newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady to up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady to up.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mostly steady to higher on Friday, supported by nearby supply tightness in several locations, dealers said.
"The market is firm. People who have something in the nearby will not trade," one Carolinas trader said.
He added that mill run times have been lower in the Carolinas as well as in Indiana.
A Buffalo dealer said most of the feed was sold earlier this week. "There is interest for extra loads. But it is a pretty thin market and kind of short on the supply side," he said.
"St. Louis feed was looking for guidance from the Southwest, particularly Kansas City," a dealer said.
"My guess is the feed business has somewhat improved and flour mills have lost a little run time," he said.

On the other hand, a Minneapolis dealer said there was ample supply. "I don't see a tightness in nearby supplies. A lot of people have outstanding supply to sell," a Minneapolis dealer said. "There is too much stuff out there."
But the dealer said there was very little forward contracting. "People are waiting for corn and millfeed prices to go down," the dealer said.
